findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the recorded scope with the current tree: confirm whether the three mcp-client-pat-* import blocks (ssm.tf:203-216) are effective, restate the true adds/changes/destroys count, and correct the '6 adds' / 'three import blocks already adopted' assertions if the mcp-PAT adoptions reduce the create count.
evidence: Plan: 'The three `import` blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op.'
infra/terraform/ssm.tf:203-216 declares import blocks to = aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets["/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-{copilot,codex,claude}"] — i.e. SIX import blocks (3 jira + 3 mcp), not three
ssm.tf comment lines 195-202 state the three mcp-client-pat-* slots were seeded in AWS at version 1 and these import blocks adopt them, so a plain create would otherwise fail ParameterAlreadyExists
Ticket comment 'LIVE APPLY ATTEMPTED' records the three mcp-client-pat-* creates failing ParameterAlreadyExists and change 2389 adding import blocks to fix exactly this
findings.finding: The plan's recorded scope (6 to add, incl. 'The three import blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op' and '4 new rebar_secrets SSM params for MCP client PATs') does not match the current config tree, which now carries import blocks for the three mcp-client-pat-* SecureString params at ssm.tf:203-216 (six import blocks total, not three). If those adoptions take effect against the already-seeded live params, three of the four PAT creates become no-op adoptions and the plan produces fewer than 6 adds.
findings.location: Plan body 'DEFERRED DEPLOYMENT DECISION' bullet '4 new rebar_secrets SSM params' + 'The three import blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op'; Verification bullet 'must match the approved scope: 6 adds'
scenarios: An operator runs `terraform plan` per the Verification gate and sees e.g. '4 to add' (2 alarms + mcp-tickets-pat + the 3 adopted-as-no-op mcp PATs) rather than the mandated '6 adds', and cannot reconcile plan output with the approval scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run `terraform plan` against current origin/main and update the plan's recorded envelope and the Verification 'must match' count to the actual number (accounting for the now-present mcp-client-pat-* import blocks at ssm.tf:203-216), or explicitly note which creates are expected to resolve to no-op adoptions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the approved plan scope by running `terraform plan` against CURRENT origin/main (which now carries the mcp-client-pat import blocks at ssm.tf:203-215 and the value_wo secret contract at ssm.tf:95-110) and state the observed add/change/destroy counts, rather than pinning the decision to the earlier recorded 6/1/0 shape.
evidence: Plan: 'The pending terraform plan ... reports Plan: 6 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy: ... 4 new rebar_secrets SSM params for MCP client PATs. The three import blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op.'
ssm.tf:203-215 defines import blocks for mcp-client-pat-copilot/codex/claude (added after the recorded plan, per dd30 'APPLY ATTEMPTED' comment where those 3 creates failed ParameterAlreadyExists)
ssm.tf:95-110: all secret slots now use value_wo/value_wo_version, not the value=CHANGEME + ignore_changes contract the recorded plan predates
Verification: 'terraform plan in infra/terraform must match the approved scope: 6 adds, 1 in-place ... change, and 0 destroys.'
findings.finding: The plan's recorded plan shape (6 add / 1 change / 0 destroy, with '4 new rebar_secrets SSM params for MCP client PATs' created and only the 3 Jira import blocks adopted) is stale: current origin/main ssm.tf already carries import blocks for the three mcp-client-pat-* params (ssm.tf:203-215) and has migrated every secret slot to write-only value_wo (ssm.tf:95-110). A fresh `terraform plan` on current main will therefore not produce the same add/change counts, so the Verification gate that requires the fresh plan to 'match the approved scope' can misfire.
findings.location: Plan body 'DEFERRED DEPLOYMENT DECISION' bullet list; Verification bullet 1
scenarios: Operator re-runs terraform plan on current main before applying and sees a different add/change count than 6/1/0, then either aborts a safe apply or is unable to certify 'matches approved scope'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria covering the Verification deliverables: the autodeploy timer was paused/re-enabled (unit name recorded) and post-apply health of Gerrit/review-bot/opcert/MCP plus one clean autodeploy cycle is confirmed.
evidence: Verification: 'Pause the discovered autodeploy systemd timer/unit for the apply window, record the exact unit name in a ticket comment, then re-enable it.'
Verification: 'After apply, verify Gerrit, review-bot, opcert, and MCP health and confirm the autodeploy timer completes one clean cycle.'
ACs list only: operator reviews/approves-or-rejects, and (if approved) apply performed with state recorded
findings.finding: Two Verification-section deliverables — pausing/re-enabling the autodeploy timer and recording its unit name, and the post-apply health verification — are described work with no covering acceptance criterion (the ACs cover only the approve/reject decision and recording resulting state).
scenarios: An executor marks the ticket done on operator approval + apply without confirming the timer was re-enabled or that health checks passed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan: capture the pre-apply terraform state and the prior user_data revision, and state the revert procedure (and success check) to run if the apply or post-apply health verification fails.
evidence: 'in-place update of aws_instance.gerrit user_data' — an in-place instance user_data change can disrupt or replace the running Gerrit service
'After apply, verify Gerrit, review-bot, opcert, and MCP health' states a check but no action if the check FAILS
T4 remedy requires an explicit rollback/back-out or expand-contract mechanism, not acknowledgement + health-check alone
findings.finding: The plan performs a destructive/impactful prod terraform apply (in-place user_data update to aws_instance.gerrit plus new SSM secrets) but states no explicit rollback / back-out plan if the apply fails or if post-apply health checks fail.
scenarios: The apply succeeds but Gerrit fails its post-apply health check and the operator has no defined revert path
A partial apply leaves SSM params or alarms created but the instance in a bad state
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Verification: 'Before apply, snapshot current terraform state; on failed apply or failed health check, revert user_data to <prior commit> and re-apply, then re-run the Gerrit/review-bot/opcert/MCP health checks.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition if the apply fails partway or post-apply health checks fail: rollback/re-apply/leave-paused, and whether the autodeploy timer is re-enabled before or after remediation.
evidence: Plan alters a deploy path (in-place `aws_instance.gerrit` user_data change + 6 adds) and pauses/re-enables the autodeploy timer
Verification enumerates only the success outcome; no stated action if apply errors mid-run or health checks fail
A 6-add/1-change apply that partially fails leaves indeterminate state with no stated recovery disposition
findings.finding: The Verification section defines the success path (health checks pass, timer completes one clean cycle) but states no disposition if the `terraform apply` fails partway or if the post-apply health checks fail — no rollback/re-apply/partial-state contract.
findings.location: Verification — 'After apply, verify Gerrit, review-bot, opcert, and MCP health and confirm the autodeploy timer completes one clean cycle.'
scenarios: apply fails after creating some resources but before the user_data change lands — no stated rollback leaves the instance in a mixed state
post-apply MCP health check fails — no stated disposition (roll back? re-apply? leave timer paused?)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Verification/rollback line: on apply error or failed health check, keep the autodeploy timer paused, capture the partial state, and record the remediation (rollback vs re-apply) on the ticket before re-enabling the timer.

Credentials with no defined retirement path accumulate/leak as clients change
findings.finding: The plan introduces 4 new SSM `rebar_secrets` params holding MCP client PATs (credential state) but defines no rotation/retirement/ownership lifecycle for them — who owns rotation, and how they are retired when a client is decommissioned.
findings.location: DEFERRED DEPLOYMENT DECISION — '4 new rebar_secrets SSM params for MCP client PATs'
scenarios: A decommissioned MCP client's PAT stays live in SSM indefinitely because no retire path was defined
Ambiguity over who may rotate the PATs leads to stale or unrotated credentials
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note stating who owns/rotates the PATs and how they are removed when a client is retired, or cite the upstream plan section that already specifies it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the plan that seeded SSM SecureString values are protected by the write-only `value_wo`/`value_wo_version` contract (ssm.tf:95-105, ADR 0105), and add a post-apply verification that the live values of the seeded secrets (esp. the three `mcp-client-pat-*` and the jira-api-token) are unchanged.
evidence: Plan lists '4 new rebar_secrets SSM params for MCP client PATs' as in-scope but says nothing about secret-value preservation for the apply.

Parent ticket comments repeatedly flag: 'a clean apply currently shares one physical apply with the value_wo secrets migration on ssm.tf, which would overwrite prod SecureString values with CHANGEME'.
ssm.tf:104-105 `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` / `value_wo_version = 1` — write-only, never persisted to state; the provider re-sends only on a version bump.
Verification checks add/change/destroy COUNTS but not secret-value integrity.
findings.finding: The plan authorizes a prod `terraform apply` but never states or verifies that the operator-seeded SSM SecureString VALUES survive the apply — the dominant recurring hazard across the parent ticket (an apply reverting ~21 live prod SecureStrings to the `CHANGEME` placeholder). On current origin/main this is neutralized by the write-only `value_wo`/`value_wo_version` contract (ssm.tf:95-105, ADR 0105), which stores only the version integer and re-sends the secret only when the version changes — but the plan neither names this protection nor adds a check for it, so a reviewer/operator cannot confirm the historically-feared clobber cannot happen.
scenarios: Operator approves the apply believing count-matching is sufficient, unaware whether any SSM value is rewritten.
A future re-plan from a tree predating the value_wo contract silently reintroduces the CHANGEME-overwrite path and the count check does not catch it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a post-apply Verification step confirming the three `mcp-client-pat-*` SecureStrings adopted with no `ParameterAlreadyExists` error and appear no-op/adopted in `terraform state`, mirroring the jira import-block adoption evidence.
evidence: Parent ticket: 'aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets[".../mcp-client-pat-copilot"] — Error 400 ParameterAlreadyExists' on the prior apply.
ssm.tf:203-215 now carries the three mcp-client-pat import blocks that fix that collision.
Plan Verification confirms MCP health but not the adoption/no-collision outcome for these three params specifically.
findings.finding: The post-apply Verification checks 'MCP health' but does not explicitly confirm the three already-live `mcp-client-pat-*` SecureStrings were ADOPTED cleanly (no `ParameterAlreadyExists` failure, values intact) — the exact partial-apply failure the parent ticket's earlier apply attempt hit before the import blocks landed at ssm.tf:203-215.
scenarios: Re-plan run from a tree missing the import blocks; apply fails partway on ParameterAlreadyExists and leaves a mixed state.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, as an explicit apply precondition, that the three `/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-{claude,codex,copilot}` import blocks must be present in the applied tree (else the apply errors `ParameterAlreadyExists` partway), and have the operator confirm their presence before authorizing apply.
evidence: Plan text names only the THREE Jira import blocks as no-op: 'The three import blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op.'

Ticket comment 'LIVE APPLY ATTEMPTED': the three `mcp-client-pat-*` creates returned 'Error 400 ParameterAlreadyExists' because they 'already exist in AWS at version 1 with NO import block'; post-apply re-plan showed residual 'Plan: 3 to add'.

The apply's clean completion is an asserted external capability the plan depends on but does not verify or gate on the mcp-client-pat import blocks being present (change 2389 pending Submit per a later comment).
findings.finding: The plan directs an operator to apply the recorded `6 add / 1 change / 0 destroy` plan but does not name the documented apply-time failure: three `mcp-client-pat-*` SecureString creates collide with pre-existing AWS parameters unless matching import blocks are landed, so a `terraform apply` of this scope errors `ParameterAlreadyExists` partway.
findings.location: Plan body ('The three import blocks in the plan are already adopted as no-op') and Verification bullet 1
scenarios: Operator approves the plan on the stated scope, runs apply, and it fails partway on ParameterAlreadyExists — after the Gerrit stop/start has already occurred.
Apply leaves the tree in a partially-applied state requiring manual reconciliation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition to Verification: `grep 'to = aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets\["/rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat' *.tf` returns all three import blocks; if absent, block the apply until they are landed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a value_wo precondition to Verification: confirm the applied tree does NOT carry an unseeded `value_wo` migration on `ssm.tf` (or require an in-window re-seed of all real secret values), since a write-only change is invisible in the `6 add/1 change/0 destroy` summary the gate relies on.
evidence: Final ticket comment: 'a clean apply here now shares the SAME physical apply as the `value_wo` migration on origin/main:ssm.tf, which would overwrite all 21 prod SecureString secrets with the CHANGEME placeholder (write-only arg, invisible in the plan diff) -> prod auth/signing/reconcile outage.'
ssm.tf:100-105 declares `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` / `value_wo_version = 1` — an ADR-0105 write-only argument the provider does not surface as an in-place change in the add/change/destroy count.
The plan offers no check that would detect a value_wo mutation, so the stated gate cannot falsify this hazard.
findings.finding: The plan's approval/verification gate keys entirely on the plan summary `6 add / 1 change / 0 destroy`, but a write-only `value_wo` SSM change is invisible in that summary; the ticket record states a clean apply now shares one physical apply with the value_wo migration that would overwrite all 21 prod SecureString values with `CHANGEME`.
findings.location: Verification bullet 1 ('must match the approved scope: 6 adds, 1 in-place ... change, and 0 destroys')
scenarios: Operator verifies the counts match, approves, and the same apply silently overwrites live prod secrets with CHANGEME, causing an auth/signing/reconcile outage.
The apply's blast radius exceeds what the plan's own verification gate can observe.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference the value_wo cutover ticket (097b-de23-bf12-4c38) as a hard prerequisite and require inspecting `terraform show -json` / value_wo_version deltas rather than trusting the add/change/destroy counts alone.
